scope: Publish only the version that was approved.

sources.A: Author edits; approver approves a specific version; publisher can release only approved versions.
sources.B: Approver approves v1. Author makes a substantive v2 edit. Publisher opens v2.
sources.C: The release view shows v1 approval separately and marks v2 unapproved; publishing v2 is blocked until its approval.

exclusions: Real delivery reliability and human behavior are outside this bounded model.

scope: A transfers a support case to B.

sources.A: A can assign a case to the B queue. B can accept queued cases; the dispatcher can recover stalled transfers.
sources.B: The fixture establishes that B has not accepted at the end of this trace. A queue notice is delivered.
sources.C: Assignment clears A as owner immediately; no owner is defined until B accepts.

exclusions: Real delivery reliability and human behavior are outside this bounded model.

scope: B completes a decision using a private rationale.

sources.A: A may read a private rationale. B may decide using only a disclosed summary; B cannot read the private rationale.
sources.B: The decision requires the summary. A remains the owner until B can act.
sources.C: No summary disclosure surface or event is specified.

exclusions: Real delivery reliability and human behavior are outside this bounded model.

scope: Resolve an assigned request despite an absent approver.

sources.A: Approver may decide assigned requests. Dispatcher may reassign to an authorized alternate.
sources.B: The approver is absent for this entire trace; requester waits on a pending request.
sources.C: No observer, timeout, escalation or return event is specified for the pending wait.

exclusions: Real delivery reliability and human behavior are outside this bounded model.

scope: A transfers a support case to B.

sources.A: A can assign a case to the B queue. B can accept queued cases; the dispatcher can recover stalled transfers.
sources.B: The fixture establishes that B has not accepted at the end of this trace. A queue notice is delivered.
sources.C: A remains accountable until B accepts; after 30 elapsed minutes the dispatcher sees and owns an unaccepted transfer.

exclusions: Real delivery reliability and human behavior are outside this bounded model.

scope: Recover a failed workflow after a physical dispatch.

sources.A: Dispatch is irreversible in this fixture. A service may flag cancellation; an operator can arrange return or record unrecoverable dispatch.
sources.B: Dispatch completes, then receipt recording fails.
sources.C: Receipt failure creates a recovery task owned by the operator; dispatch remains recorded as occurred. Operator arranges return or records unrecoverable dispatch, and communicates the outcome to the authorized requester.

exclusions: Real delivery reliability and human behavior are outside this bounded model.

scope: Requester reads a committed decision in a single authenticated session.

sources.A: Requester can view their request; assigned approver can decide. All actions in this fixture pass authorization.
sources.B: Approver commits v1 approval; requester then explicitly reads the current v1 decision page. The page shows Approved and no further required action.
sources.C: Approval is terminal. No edits, departure, notification, external effect or subsequent action is in scope.

exclusions: Notification transport, later revisions and user behavior outside the trace.

scope: Resolve an assigned request despite an absent approver.

sources.A: Approver may decide assigned requests. Dispatcher may reassign to an authorized alternate.
sources.B: The approver is absent for this entire trace; requester waits on a pending request.
sources.C: After 60 elapsed minutes a service timer exposes the pending wait to dispatcher, who owns recovery and reassigns to an authorized alternate; the request stays pending until a decision.

exclusions: Real delivery reliability and human behavior are outside this bounded model.
